runs.content: SAP SE picked up at the previous close ($209.14) — a ~31% discount to Morningstar's $302 wide-moat fair value, with cloud backlog +27% YoY and full-year cloud guidance reaffirmed despite a trimmed operating-profit guide and a Buy→Neutral downgrade (PT raised to €201). BR was exited discretionarily (−8.18%, −$82) to keep the book at 35 open positions after SAP's entry — no mechanical stop-losses or signal exits on the other 33 continuing positions amid a second consecutive oil-driven risk-off session (Brent >$100/bbl on Iran-conflict escalation). RELX is now the weakest continuing position at −6.55%, no Burry conflict. Portfolio net P&L: +$1,835 (+3.16% on $58,000).

Lockheed Martin picked up at the previous close ($536.15) — entered on a same-day UBS upgrade to Buy (PT $674 from $581, missile-segment revenue +150% 2025-2030) tied directly to fresh Iran/Saudi Arabia strikes pushing oil toward 3-month highs and a broad risk-off tape (Dow −600pts). TRV was exited discretionarily (−7.95%, −$79) to keep the book at 35 open positions after LMT's entry — no mechanical stop-losses or signal exits on the other 33 continuing positions; AMGN fell −9.0% intraday on a Novartis Lp(a) trial-failure read-through (sector-wide biotech selling) but stayed net positive and was held. BR is now the weakest continuing position at −7.90%, no Burry conflict. Portfolio net P&L: +$2,055 (+3.60% on $57,000).
